title: Vehicle Safety Checks: Show Me, Tell Me
whatItIs: On the car test the examiner asks one 'tell me' question before the drive and one 'show me' question on the move, from the list in DT1. Basic knowledge is enough.
keyFacts: One 'tell me' before moving away; one 'show me' while driving, on a suitable road.
One or both answered wrongly = one driving fault on a car test.
A serious or dangerous loss of control during the 'show me' is marked at 'Vehicle checks'.
Show me: washers and wipers, dipped headlights, rear demister, horn, front demist, side window.
Candidates aren't asked to touch a hot engine or check fluids by hand. The car's information system may be used.

visual.caption: Tell me: what a good answer includes

rows: Not spongy or slack; test as you set off; no pulling to one side
Manufacturer's guide; reliable gauge; check cold; spare; refit valve caps
No cuts or bulges; 1.6 mm across the central 3/4, all the way round
Rigid part at least as high as the eye or top of the ears; close to the head
Gentle pressure on the wheel as the engine starts, or turn just after moving off
Press the pedal; use reflections in windows or doors, or ask a helper
Dipstick min/max; header tank high/low marks; reservoir high/low marks

a.label: Tell me
points: Explain the check: no need to do it

b.label: Show me
points: Operate the control without losing control

onTheTest.question: How should a head restraint be adjusted to give the best protection in a crash?
options: Rigid part at least as high as the eye or top of the ears
Level with the base of the neck
As far from the head as possible
Rigid part level with the shoulders
onTheTest.why: DT1 13.01 (T3): the rigid part should be at least as high as the eye or top of the ears, and as close to the back of the head as is comfortable.

onTheTest.question: A candidate answers the 'tell me' wrongly, then does the 'show me' correctly with no loss of control. What's recorded?
onTheTest.why: DT1 section 11: on a car test, one or both questions answered incorrectly results in one driving fault.

traps: Two wrong answers is still only one driving fault on a car test.
ABS warning light comes on? That shows a fault with the anti-lock braking system.
Opening the bonnet isn't a test competence, but instructors are expected to teach it.
